articles.title: Teal Hex Haze
articles.summary: Soft blurred teal and grey haze with faint hexagon hints, like fogged glass. A smooth dark-to-light teal and sage gradient with a faint hex facet texture; it looks like a soft misty backdrop, like pixelated fog.
articles.what: Real-source pattern plate cropped to 2048 with paired image-derived dynamic spec channels. Up close: A low-poly mosaic of flat-tone hexagons about 40 px across, each one a single solid colour that steps gently from its neighbour. Colours flow from near-black green at the lower left through deep teal and sage to pale cream-white at the upper right. Edges are crisp, with no grain. From a distance: A smooth dark-to-light teal and sage gradient with a faint hex facet texture; it looks like a soft misty backdrop, like pixelated fog. Measured spec (average): metal 65, roughness 118, coat 144. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Teal Hex Haze" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: the gradient needs a long run
Dark end at the rear or low on the body for a natural fade
Mid-tone plate: dark green or black numbers read on the light end, white on the dark end; plain mid-teal numbers vanish.
Almost nothing: it is a source plate artwork with its own gradient, keep a clean plate for numbers
Pairs well with: white, silver, mint, charcoal.
pitfalls: Not a blurred fog: hexagons have crisp edges and flat tones
Not a loud pattern: low contrast between neighbours
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 65 (pearl-level metal), roughness 118 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 144 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: it is a source plate artwork with its own gradient, keep a clean plate for numbers; at most a thin white or black pinstripe
Patterns to avoid: other hex, honeycomb or mosaic patterns: collide with the tiles; fine flake and noise: ruin the clean facets
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: glassy facets; none: the spec already follows the plate
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Terracotta Ceramic Grid
articles.summary: Warm terracotta basket-weave grid, flat matte clay tiles with faint sparkle. Reads as a warm clay-pink brown with a faint tiled grid; from far it is almost a solid dusty terracotta.
articles.what: Real-source pattern plate cropped to 2048 with paired image-derived dynamic spec channels. Up close: A mosaic of square and rectangular tiles about 15-30 px, in slightly different shades of terracotta pink-brown, divided by thin pale cream-yellow grout lines. Tile shades vary only a little; it is low contrast and flat, with no weave. From a distance: Reads as a warm clay-pink brown with a faint tiled grid; from far it is almost a solid dusty terracotta. Measured spec (average): metal 73, roughness 173, coat 124. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, gt / sports car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Terracotta Ceramic Grid" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: All body panels: even all-over mosaic
Roof and hood show the grid best
Low contrast: white, cream or black numbers read well; terracotta-toned ones disappear.
Large bold graphics, stripes and lettering: the quiet grid stays under them
Pairs well with: cream, dark brown, black, olive.
pitfalls: Not basket weave: the old card says woven, it is a flat tile mosaic with grout lines
Not shiny glazed ceramic: semi-matte, low metal
Avoid: small numbers over the fine grid, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 73 (pearl-level metal), roughness 173 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 124 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the fine grid, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold graphics, stripes and lettering: the quiet grid stays under them; a cream or dark brown stripe
Patterns to avoid: other grid, weave or mosaic patterns: moire; fine glitter

Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Tokyo Script Textile
articles.summary: Charcoal cloth covered in red and white Chinese characters, dense and dark. Reads as a dark charcoal car covered in red and white calligraphy, like a Tokyo street sign collage; busy, high contrast, mostly red on dark.
articles.what: Real-source pattern plate cropped to 2048 with paired image-derived dynamic spec channels. Up close: Brush-script Japanese kanji in coral red and white scattered over dark green-charcoal, characters 20-90 px tall, with a few red seal stamps and small grey chop marks. Words include sushi, tea and the four seasons. The tile repeats about every 250 px, so identical characters appear again and again. From a distance: Reads as a dark charcoal car covered in red and white calligraphy, like a Tokyo street sign collage; busy, high contrast, mostly red on dark. Measured spec (average): metal 82, roughness 165, coat 125. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, sides, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Tokyo Script Textile" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Sides, doors and hood: repeating text reads as wallpaper on any panel
Avoid small trim; characters become fragments
Too busy for numbers; use a solid white or black plate behind them.
Almost nothing: it is finished artwork; a plate for numbers is the only add-on
Pairs well with: red, white, black, gold.
pitfalls: Not Chinese: the old card says Chinese characters, the render has Japanese kanji such as sushi and tea
Not a single poster: it repeats every 250 px, so panels carry a full grid of characters
Avoid: numbers over the text, large dark areas in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 82 (pearl-level metal), roughness 165 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 125 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers over the text, large dark areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: it is finished artwork; a plate for numbers is the only add-on; a plain white or red pinline border
Patterns to avoid: any other pattern, camo, flake or glitter; a second text or graphic layer
Spec overlays that work: none needed; a gloss clear patch if you want the ink to pop
